CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.summary:
Independently verified TEST-DESIGNER's Step 3 mutation-strengthening pass on REQ-170's suite. All 7 requirement acceptance criteria (AC1-AC7, docs/requirements.yaml) map to at least one runnable, passing test per test/specs/REQ-170.md's traceability table, cross-checked directly against the test source: AC1/AC3/AC4 in plugin_handler_test.exs, AC2/AC5/AC6 in call_timeout_test.exs, AC7 discharged by this validator's own compile/test runs. No @tag :skip, no 'TODO: implement test' anywhere in either file. No hardcoded secrets/connection strings. Each test builds its own ExecutionContext via a per-test Ecto.UUID.generate() helper, no shared hardcoded IDs; both files run async: false by design (real Wasmtime NIF instances) but no test depends on another test's side effects -- each is self-sufficient.

Independently re-applied 2 of the 4 genuinely-new-gap mutations myself (not just read the report): (1) M6 -- plugin_handler.ex call_export/3 changed to call Wasmex.call_function/4 as 3-arity (dropping timeout_ms, falling back to wasmex's hardcoded 5000ms default). Ran mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler_test.exs: 12/14 passed, 2 failed, including the M6-closing test ('timeout_ms longer than wasmex's hardcoded 5_000ms default still governs the wait') with elapsed_ms=5003 (fails the >6_000 assertion) -- confirms the reported pass/fail behavior exactly. Reverted via git checkout --, confirmed git status --porcelain lib/ empty. (2) M7 -- call_timeout.ex moduledoc replaced with an adversarial bakery-staffing paragraph scattering every AC6 keyword (OQ-5, NOT settled by this requirement, load spike, S6, worker-pool-exhaustion, node-global, filed, DIVERGENCE, decision 0014, does **not** hold) out of context. Ran mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout_test.exs: 15/16 passed, exactly 1 failed -- the new strengthened test ('the OQ-5 filing and DIVERGENCE claims cite the actual mechanism terms and design doc...'), failing on 'assert moduledoc =~ "TOKIO_RUNTIME"'; the 3 pre-existing loose AC6 tests all passed against the adversarial doc, exactly matching the reported gap. Reverted via git checkout --, confirmed git status --porcelain lib/ empty and a follow-up mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/ run green (98 passed) after both reverts.

Confirmed call_timeout.ex and plugin_handler.ex are byte-identical to their pre-TEST-DESIGNER-pass state: git diff e60c1db -- lib/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout.ex lib/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler.ex is empty, and git log e60c1db..HEAD for those two paths shows no commits (TEST-DESIGNER's commit c20928b only touched the decision doc and handoff files, matching its own claim).

Confirmed docs/migration/decisions/0014-scripting-plugin-runtime-strategy.md's correction is internally consistent: the new WASM-11 correction paragraph under 'Reasoning (a)' (point ii/iii) is present; WASM-11 was removed from the 'Requirements judged satisfiable substantially as worded' list and a new WASM-11 entry added inside the 'Requirements NOT satisfiable as literally worded' section (verified by line-range check, entry falls between that header at line 376 and the next header 'Open questions' at line 595); the REQ-VALIDATOR restatement watchlist was updated to include WASM-11 with a dated note; and OQ-5 carries a matching amendment citing the same live-verified TOKIO_RUNTIME worker-pool-exhaustion finding. No contradiction found between the correction's claims and the rest of the file.

mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/ (real output, this validator's own run, post-revert): 'Finished in 12.8 seconds (0.00s async, 12.8s sync)\n\nResult: 98 passed'. WASMEX_BUILD=true mix compile --warnings-as-errors: exit 0, no output (clean).

VERDICT: PASS. No coverage gaps found; TEST-DESIGNER's report was not overclaiming on the 2 mutations spot-checked.
